survey: A cartoon meteor in flight. Main parts: (1) A lumpy brown-grey rock body, centered and turned slightly toward the camera. Its front face, at lower left, has one large crater, two medium craters and a few small pits. (2) A fire trail of three orange flame lobes that grows from the rock's upper-right back edge and streams up and to the right. The rock is lit warm orange where the flames meet it. The flame tips end in small round sparks. The flames point away from the direction of travel, which is lower left, so the trail sits behind the rock where it belongs. Nothing needs support because the meteor is meant to be in flight against an abstract background. The craters are shaped like real impact craters: rims, sunken bowls and sensible sizes. The rock is one solid mass with no parts melting into or passing through each other. The flames and sparks are the normal stylized trail of a burning meteor, not invented parts. Three lobes plus sparks is an accepted game-card simplification.
